prompt: Some people think that educated people are more valuable than people who have learned skills through experience. Do you think that educated people are the most valuable for society? What kinds of skills can people learn through experience that can benefit society?
essay:
Formal education plays an important role in preparing people for many professions, but I do not believe that educated individuals are necessarily more valuable to society than those who have developed practical skills through experience. In my view, a successful society depends on both academic knowledge and hands-on expertise, because each contributes in different ways.

People with formal qualifications are essential in fields where specialist knowledge is required. Doctors, engineers, teachers and lawyers, for example, need extensive education before they can perform their roles safely and effectively. Their academic training enables them to understand complex theories, apply established principles and make informed decisions. However, qualifications alone do not guarantee practical competence. In many occupations, experience is equally important because it teaches people how to deal with real situations, solve unexpected problems and adapt their knowledge to different circumstances.

Experience can also develop a wide range of skills that are highly valuable to society. Practical abilities such as construction, repair work, farming and machinery operation are often learned largely through repeated practice rather than classroom study. In addition, people can develop communication, leadership and problem-solving skills through years of working with others. For instance, an experienced tradesperson may be able to identify and fix a technical problem quickly, while a long-serving supervisor may know how to manage conflict and motivate a team effectively. These skills contribute directly to the functioning of communities and workplaces.

In conclusion, educated people are undoubtedly valuable, particularly in professions that require specialist knowledge, but they should not be regarded as more valuable than those who have learned through experience. Society benefits most when academic knowledge is combined with practical ability, judgement and interpersonal skills developed in real-life situations.
